title: Collatz matrix obstructions, synchronization, and basin densities: three papers and Lean artifacts
description:
Three standalone papers with LaTeX sources, PDFs, Lean proof sources, and verification reports: (1) Two-coordinate obstructions for affine interpretations of the Yolcu–Aaronson–Heule Collatz system; (2) An independent second proof of Said Duran’s equal-height Collatz runs theorem; (3) Collatz basin densities and canonical traces from first-passage stabilization.

The matrix and synchronization scope has 137 checked Lean modules and 633 public theorem/lemma declarations. The native basin bundle has 1,602 bundled Lean modules, including 281 local proof modules, 1,507 local theorem/lemma declarations, 275 definitions and named instances, and 5 separately audited upstream roots; its root audit checks 1,787 declarations. The actual first-passage inputs at alpha=1001/1000 and alpha=2001/2000 are connected to basin and label densities, first-hit clocks, Green limits, and cylinder Cesàro/Abel identification. Mazur’s separate natural-counting and predecessor theorems give natural-density limits and positivity at targets prime to three. The global sublinearity and eventual-periodicity conditions are proved equivalent, but neither is established. Additional cycles remain unexcluded. None of these papers proves the Collatz conjecture. Priority for the equal-height existence theorem belongs to Omar Javier Said Duran.

The recorded joint build distinguishes fresh compilation from exact dependency-checked object reuse. The default native verifier rebuilds all bundled modules. All audited roots use only the standard Lean axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

Original code, scripts, and documentation use MIT. Imported formal sources in external/ and formal-basins-native/ retain their own licenses and separate Mazur, Advameg, and upstream notices; the source-license map identifies the Apache-2.0 packages. Papers and their LaTeX sources and PDFs use CC BY 4.0; code excerpts retain their code licenses. Third-party material retains its original rights. This DOI archives the complete repository release, containing the three individually titled papers.
